tools.name: manage_archive
tools.title: Novel Archive Management
tools.description: Manage Novel archival and checkpoint surfaces. Export writes a file; import writes Novel state and mode selects dry-run (validate only), merge (keep existing entries), or replace (discard current Novel state), while strict aborts on unresolved references. archive is reversible with unarchive; checkpoint_restore replaces the live Novel with the stored checkpoint and is itself undoable; checkpoint subscriptions persist. Use when: exporting or importing a Novel, archiving/unarchiving, cloning/branching, or managing checkpoints. Do NOT use when: creating, resuming, renaming, or ending a Novel — use manage_novel. Revert the most recent mutation with manage_history (action: undo); checkpoint_list is read-only.

tools.description: Manage per-entity evidence, reconciled belief stances, the perception ledger, and a one-entity knowledge query. admit records a subject/predicate/object proposition with a 0..1 weight and does not change a stance until reconcile recomputes it; retract removes the cited evidence and reconciles; the perception ledger is append-only, so correct a mistaken perception with a new record. Mutating actions persist to the Novel; reads are read-only. knowledge_query returns perceptions, beliefs, and known secrets with event provenance, optionally filtered by topic. tools.name: manage_staging
tools.title: Scene Staging Management
tools.description: Manage scene presence, autonomy, and social-cast staging. presence replaces the present set; cast sets the multi-NPC speaker strategy with mute/unmute adjusting its pool; next_speaker runs manual, forced, or pooled selection, where force overrides select; autonomy changes apply to the current scene only. Presence, autonomy, and cast state persist to the Novel and are audited. Use when: setting who is present, adjusting scene autonomy, choosing a speaker strategy, or selecting the next speaker. Do NOT use when: setting the scene, issuing a directive, offering choices, or consulting the oracle — use manage_scene. Revert the most recent mutation with manage_history (action: undo).

params.after_user: Reset the pooled spoken-set for a new user turn (next_speaker).
params.force: NPC forced as the next speaker (cast/next_speaker).
params.select: NPC selected as the manual speaker (cast/next_speaker).

tools.name: manage_story
tools.title: Story Journal Management
tools.description: Manage the story journal — typed narrative memories (decision, moment, revelation, bond, consequence). record appends an entry and consumes the turn_handle minted by take_turn; update edits a mutable entry; decision and consequence entries are immutable and refuse update or promotion; remove deletes an entry by index; promote copies an entry into lore under a derived or supplied key. list filters by type and paginates with offset and limit, returning previews unless detail is set. Mutations require the GM or Editor badge, persist to the Novel, and are undoable via manage_history (action: undo); list is read-only. Use when: recording, editing, removing, listing, or promoting story beats. Do NOT use when: recording a durable world fact — use manage_lore (action: set).

params.turn_handle: Turn handle minted by take_turn (record); consumed on success.

tools.name: manage_synthesis
tools.title: Synthesis Management
tools.description: Manage synthesis content (voice examples, lore templates, action patterns, and other Ruleset Wisdom). Mutating actions (run, revert, activate, deactivate, toggle, toggle_action, player_add, player_remove, record_ruling, revert_ruling) persist to the Novel and are audited; read-only actions (list, player_list, verify) do not mutate state. verify checks each item's stored citation locally and reports pass/weak/unsupported; it never fetches and never changes state. record_ruling writes a ruling and its verified citations to the GM-only ruling ledger; revert_ruling marks a ledger entry reverted; ruling_list reads the ledger newest-first. Undo the latest mutation with manage_history. activate/deactivate with key omitted act on the whole module. Use when: running, reverting, listing, activating, deactivating, toggling, verifying, recording or reading rulings, or player-authoring items. Do NOT use when: browsing the codex — use manage_codex (action: list).

params.max_entries: Maximum rulings to return, newest first (ruling_list; default 20).

tools.name: manage_vow
tools.title: Vow Management
tools.description: Track narrative vows, quests, and obligations with milestones. set creates a vow and links a countdown whose ticks follow the difficulty rank track (scope defaults to shared); milestone advances progress; resolve and forsake close the vow with distinct outcomes (fulfilled vs abandoned). Mutations require the GM or Editor badge, persist to the Novel, and are undoable via manage_history (action: undo); resolve and forsake are terminal in the forward direction. Use when: setting, advancing, resolving, forsaking, or listing vows. Do NOT use when: starting a clock timer — use manage_countdown (action: set).

params.difficulty: troublesome, dangerous, formidable, extreme, or epic (set).
params.name: Vow name (set).

tools.name: manage_world
tools.title: World Model Management
tools.description: Manage the world model — rooms, things, exits, and their spatial properties. create and update mutate in place and persist to the Novel; all mutations are audited; remove is permanent and requires re-creation; convert replaces the described subtree; generate creates rooms from installed table pools bounded by TTRPG_WORLD_GEN_MAX_ROOMS. create_exit links both directions; create_thing honors location_type only when location is set, and kind forces property defaults. There are no read-only actions here; inspect state with run_command (action: execute). Use when: creating, updating, removing, bulk-converting, or generating locations and objects. Do NOT use when: navigating the world — use run_command (action: execute); proposing objective-state transitions — use manage_causality; recording what an entity believes — use manage_belief.

tools.name: resolve_mechanic
tools.title: Resolve Mechanics
tools.description: Resolve uncertain actions across the host's base mechanics: Fate Fudge dice, aspects, Fate points, and stress; Ironsworn momentum, moves, and progress; Forged action rolls, stress, trauma, and downtime; and generic ruleset table rolls. Rolls and state changes persist to the Novel and are audited; a roll with no following write is flagged as an uncommitted roll. Revert the most recent mutation with manage_history (action: undo). fate_roll uses dF, ironsworn_move compares an action die against two challenge dice, and forged_action_roll takes the highest of a d6 pool. Use when: resolving a Fate, Ironsworn, or Forged mechanic, or rolling on a ruleset generation table. Do NOT use when: resolving a ruleset skill check — use the bound ruleset's roll tools; managing vows — use manage_vow (action: set).

params.burn: Burn momentum to replace the action score (ironsworn_move).
params.cost: Stress cost to resist (forged_stress); defaults to 2.
params.dice: Fudge dice notation (fate_roll) or dice pool size (forged_action_roll).
params.entity_id: Entity or NPC id (fate_aspect, fate_point, fate_stress, ironsworn_momentum, ironsworn_move, forged_stress, forged_downtime).

tools.name: respond_decision
tools.title: Respond to Workflow Decision
tools.description: Answer a pending workflow decision, atomically draining it and persisting the outcome to the Novel. option must match one of the emitted choices; 'cancel' aborts the workflow and restores its pre-workflow snapshot, while any applied outcome is not reversible. The drain is mutating and audited, and a second call with no pending decision returns STATE_CONFLICT. Use when: the server emitted a [NEED_INPUT] prompt and the caller must choose. Do NOT use when: no decision is pending — use set_badge or a state tool instead.

params.decision: The canonical decision text the workflow is waiting on.
params.option: The chosen option, or 'cancel' to abort the workflow and restore its snapshot.

tools.name: run_command
tools.title: Parser Command
tools.description: Run the spatial parser: execute a parsed command, resolve a movement outcome, or map an intent to tool calls. execute accepts free-form text, mutates world and entity state, persists, and is audited; a mistaken move is reversed by issuing the inverse command because no undo snapshot is taken. resolve computes the same movement without mutating, and suggest returns recommended calls without executing them; source and target apply only to perception queries. On a ruleset-bound Novel the parser is GM-only for navigation and mutation, while the Player badge keeps read-only perception commands. Use when: a player or narrator takes a physical action, needs a movement outcome without mutating, or wants intent mapped to tools. Do NOT use when: the GM creates or edits the model — use manage_world; durable world facts — use manage_lore.

params.intent: The intent to resolve or map (resolve/suggest).
params.source: Observing actor for visibility/audibility (defaults to the active entity).
params.target: Actor or thing being seen or heard (visibility/audibility).

tools.name: set_badge
tools.title: Set Active Badge
tools.description: Switch the active badge to player, game_master, observer, or none (Editor), gating tool access server-side for the active Novel; always callable. The badge is per Novel and switching re-filters tools/list immediately, so a narrower badge can revoke tools mid-task and switching back restores them; badge changes are mutating session state, audited, and reversible by switching back. Use when: entering the story, spectating, or stepping away to edit. Do NOT use when: answering a pending workflow decision — use respond_decision.

params.badge: The badge to activate: player, game_master, observer, or none (Editor).

tools.name: take_turn
tools.title: Take Play Turn
tools.description: Resolve a player intent through the parser and mint a turn handle for the story record. The turn is read-only and non-persistent: no Novel state is mutated; the handle is session-scoped, single-use, and consumed by manage_story (action: record), though recording without it still works. Use when: taking a turn before recording its outcome. Do NOT use when: resolving a specific combat round — use manage_combat (action: advance); rolling a ruleset check — use resolve_mechanic (action: roll).
